title: Engine UI stack command queue and observed-state semantics
status: Static original-binary trace of stack command production, consumption and state queries. This map does not establish live ordering between independent command producers.

get_stack_data.scope: Returns all retained state strings, including forward history.

command_queue.order: The reviewed drain starts at the first array record and advances by 0x78. Stack-command records are dispatched in append order. It destroys the records and clears count afterward.
command_queue.visibility: Push and Back callbacks append commands and return without applying them. State queries read the applied stack; an immediate query after enqueueing is not completion acknowledgement.

applied_stack.push_semantics: Push discards forward history where necessary, copies the supplied string, appends it, sets current_index to count minus one and emits a state-change notification. This path does not require a declared UI model state or navigation context before accepting the string.
applied_stack.back_semantics: Back applies delta minus one to the current index at execution time, with index clamping. It carries no expected state name, owner token or compare-and-swap condition. Go is also relative and does not provide that condition.
applied_stack.current_semantics: isCurrent compares the complete state name selected by current_index through a character-folding comparison. Ancestor activity does not make an ancestor current.
applied_stack.history_semantics: has and indexOf search the full retained array. Their results alone do not distinguish an active ancestor from forward history after Back.

navigation.eligibility: A navigation context must match an applied current state and pass stack activity checks before this worker reaches input polling. This is a static control-flow finding, not a live interaction result.

integration_requirements: Record pending ownership before enqueueing a transition. Observe the requested state on a later update before showing controls that depend on it.
Track an outstanding exit command separately. Do not enqueue repeated Back commands while waiting for the first command to become visible.
Retain ownership when cancellation or teardown occurs before a queued enter has applied; a late command must not create an unowned modal state.
Exercise deferred queue application in fixtures. A synchronous mock for push and back omits the behavior established by these callbacks.

Do not claim atomic isolation from independent stack producers. A foreign Push queued before a Back can change the state that Back affects, even when an earlier query still reports the caller's own state. A JS-side current-state check does not close that execution-time race.
